judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: Footer mailing-list field: <label>Join the Mailing List</label> sits right above <input type=email aria-label="Email address" placeholder="Email address">, but the label has no for and does not wrap the input, so it is not associated. A screen reader announces 'Email address', as the claim says (true of the capture and the identical live HTML). I lean to a 1.3.1 failure: the author's visible <label>, presented as the field's label, has no programmatic relationship with the field, and the name comes from aria-label rather than visible text (a 2.5.3 concern too). But the field's name and visible placeholder already say what to enter, and the heading-like label text comes just before the field in reading order inside the same form. Competent auditors would reasonably differ on whether an unassociated label that works as a form title fails 1.3.1 when the field has a matching name, so the label is uncertain.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Footer 'Join the Mailing List' field <input type=email name=email id=sign-up-input aria-label="Email address"> with no autocomplete attribute. It collects the user's own email address, a purpose in WCAG's Input Purposes list, and HTML supports autocomplete="email" (H98). type=email gives the data type, not the user-information purpose, so 1.3.5 fails. The snapshot records Chromium's form issue FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError for this input, so the claim's Chromium remark holds too. Live HTML is unchanged.
